requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as a passive FTP destination using the scanner account from the handover and confine it to a dedicated dropbox.
requirements.summary: Node1 runs enabled vsftpd on port 21 with passive data ports 30000–30009. The scanner account has a root-owned chroot and a scanner-writable dropbox; node2 authenticated successfully and observed passive endpoints within the configured range.

requirements.requirement: Allow the scanner on node2 to upload and retrieve files, including the supplied sample scan.
requirements.summary: Node2 uploaded and retrieved the supplied sample through passive FTP. Source and retrieved SHA-256 hashes matched, both before and after node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Prevent the scanner account from accessing host files outside its dropbox confinement.
requirements.summary: The FTP root exposed only the dropbox; parent traversal remained at the confined root, changing to /etc and retrieving /etc/passwd were denied, and writing at the FTP root was denied. The chroot root remained root-owned and non-writable.
Anonymous login received FTP 530 before and after restarts, and the effective configuration records anonymous_enable=NO.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic. Node1 installed the Ubuntu Noble vsftpd package and its ssl-cert dependency without an OS or kernel upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, independently confirmed changed boot identity, and recovered service/data behavior afterward.
limitations: The handover password and injected FTP_PASSWORD were appropriately redacted, so their exact textual equality cannot be independently compared; successful scanner authentication strongly supports correct credential use.
The final lifecycle inventory does not enumerate /etc, so persistence of the configuration backup is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of a later removal command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were narrowly connected to installing/configuring FTP, correcting PAM shell eligibility, collecting bounded evidence, or executing the mandatory restart protocol. Package state remained healthy, no failed services appeared, and the only new listener was the required node1 FTP service. The sole unnecessary mutation identified was the retained /etc/vsftpd.conf.pre-dropbox backup created by cmd-b1b4bd0a643e4b6a; it was not removed and is minor rollback residue. No other unnecessary mutation is evident.
